reasons.D: Keeps the editorial 'we', the dash-broken asides and semicolon series, and the whimsical mock-formal stance of the passage, though its punchy repetitions run a touch simpler than the passage's ornate periodic sentences.
reasons.C: Long, clause-laden sentences with parenthetical asides ('so to say', 'as I recall') and a latinate, faintly ironic register come close, but the first-person 'I' and the smoother, more even flow miss the passage's knotted, participle-led syntax.
reasons.B: Has some period feel and wry humour, but leans on short, clipped sentences ('He browsed.', 'Always the same one.') and a modern punchline cadence the passage never uses.
reasons.A: Plain, modern, evenly paced prose with a reflective 'I' and no ornament, inversion or mock-heroic flourish; it reads least like the author.
